title: Two-way tables

match.reason: No bank point teaches building a two-way table with totals and reading probabilities from it at Stage 5 depth: the closest, the Year 10 conditional-probability card, focuses on conditional probability, and the others are Year 8, Year 12 or Victorian spreadsheet cards that teach different ideas or depths.

draft.title: Two-way tables
card: A two-way table records two categories at once. One category runs along the rows and the other down the columns. Each cell counts the outcomes that fit both.
Totals are written at the end of each row and column. The grand total, in the bottom right corner, is the number of all outcomes.
To find a probability, take the count you want and divide by the grand total. A row or column total gives the probability of one category on its own.
Example: 50 students, 20 Year 9 and 30 Year 10. 15 of the Year 9 students walk to school. P(Year 9 and walks) \(= \frac{15}{50} = \frac{3}{10}\).
draft.remember: Read the cell for both categories, or the total for one, and divide by the grand total.

a.q: A survey of 60 people asked about pets. 24 own a dog, 18 own a cat and 18 own neither. None of them own both. What is the probability a person owns a cat?
a.why: The cat total is 18 out of a grand total of 60, so \(\frac{18}{60} = \frac{3}{10}\). Using 42 as the total leaves out the people with neither pet.
a.clue: Divide by the grand total, not by another column.

b.q: At a Bathurst school, 100 students were asked how they travel. 35 of the 60 girls take the bus, and 25 of the 40 boys take the bus. What is the probability a student chosen at random is a boy who takes the bus?
b.why: The cell for boys who take the bus is 25, out of a grand total of 100, so \(\frac{25}{100} = \frac{1}{4}\). Using 40, the number of boys, gives \(\frac{5}{8}\), which is a different question.
b.clue: Use the cell for both categories and the grand total.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: a is 18/60 = 3/10 and b is 25/100 = 1/4, and the explanations agree with the card.
